title: How to Run Ads for a Local Business in Australia
description: How to run ads for a local business in Australia: set a budget, pick Google or Meta, lead with an offer, build the landing page and track every enquiry.
h1_main: How to Run Ads That Actually Work
dek: Ads work for a local business when five things line up: a clear offer, the right platform, creative that stops the scroll, a landing page built for that one ad, and tracking that tells you what each enquiry cost.
primary_keyword: how to run ads for a local business

faq.q: What is the best advertising for a small local business?
faq.a: For most local service businesses, Google Ads targeting local search terms is the best starting point, because it reaches people who already need you. For visual or impulse businesses like food, retail and events, Instagram and Facebook ads often work better.

faq.q: How much should a small business spend on ads?
faq.a: Work backwards from what a customer is worth and what you can afford to spend finding one. Commit to a test budget you're comfortable losing for at least four weeks, so you get enough data to make a decision.

faq.q: Why are my ads getting clicks but no enquiries?
faq.a: Usually it's the landing page or the offer, not the ad. Check that the page matches the ad, loads fast on mobile, has one clear action and shows proof. Also check that your conversion tracking is working.

faq.q: Should I run ads myself or hire someone?
faq.a: You can run a small Google or Meta campaign yourself if you're willing to learn and check it weekly. Hire help when your spend grows, when results stall, or when your time is worth more doing the actual work.

faq.q: How long until ads start working?
faq.a: You'll see clicks within days, but give a campaign about four weeks of steady spend before judging it. The ad platforms need time to learn who responds, and you need enough enquiries to see a pattern.
